units.title: AI Project Cycle in Depth
learn_paragraphs:
Professionals extend the cycle: Problem Scoping → Data Acquisition → Data
Exploration → Modelling → Evaluation → Deployment, then monitoring.
In modelling we choose between rule-based approaches (we write the rules) and
learning-based approaches (the model learns rules from data).
Deployment puts the model into real use. Monitoring checks it keeps working as data
changes.

units.title: Precision, Recall and F1
learn_paragraphs:
Precision = TP ÷ (TP + FP): of everything predicted positive, how much was right?
Recall = TP ÷ (TP + FN): of all real positives, how many did we find?
F1 score = 2 × (Precision × Recall) ÷ (Precision + Recall), a balance of both. Choose
the metric based on which error costs more.

units.did_you_know: For cancer screening, high recall matters most, so that few real cases are missed.

units.title: The NLP Pipeline
learn_paragraphs:
Text is processed in steps: sentence segmentation → tokenisation → removing
stopwords → normalising (lowercase, stemming or lemmatisation).
Bag of Words counts how often each word appears in a document, turning text into
numbers.
TF-IDF gives more weight to words that are frequent in one document but rare
across others.

units.did_you_know: Search engines have long used ideas like TF-IDF to rank which documents match a query.

units.title: Computer Vision Applications
learn_paragraphs:
CV tasks: image classification (what is in the image?), object detection (what and
where, with bounding boxes) and segmentation (which pixels belong to each object).
Applications include medical imaging, quality checks in factories, traffic monitoring
and accessibility tools for people who are blind.
Risks include surveillance and misidentification, so consent and accuracy testing are
essential.

units.title: The ML Workflow in Python
learn_paragraphs:
A typical scikit-learn workflow: load data → split into train/test → choose a model →
fit → predict → evaluate.
Overfitting means the model memorises training data and fails on new data.
Underfitting means it is too simple to learn the pattern.
Compare training and test scores to diagnose these problems.

units.title: How LLMs Work
learn_paragraphs:
LLMs are built on the transformer architecture. They are pre-trained on large text
to predict the next token, then fine-tuned to follow instructions.
Temperature controls randomness: low = focused and repeatable, high = more
creative and varied.
RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) lets an LLM look up trusted documents
before answering, reducing hallucinations.

units.title: Responsible AI and Governance
learn_paragraphs:
Responsible AI principles: fairness, transparency, explainability, privacy, safety
and human oversight.
Governments are creating rules. The EU AI Act takes a risk-based approach, and
India has issued AI governance guidelines alongside the DPDP Act.
Teams use tools like model cards to document what a model does, its data and its
limits.

units.did_you_know: The EU AI Act sorts AI uses into risk levels, with the strictest rules for high-risk uses.

units.title: AI Careers and Entrepreneurship
learn_paragraphs:
AI careers include data analyst, ML engineer, AI product manager, AI ethicist,
prompt and content designer and domain experts who use AI.
AI startups start with a real problem, a clear user, access to data and a way to
create value.
A pitch explains the problem, solution, users, impact and why your team can build it.
